steps.history: 241 frames on M42 in the windows (by the RAW's own EXIF and each frame's own plate solve): 193 long (30 s ISO 1600, the one before the firmware flash included), 48 short (2 s ISO 400); used 165 long and 44 short. Darks: none: darks.subtract changed nothing and said so; hot pixels found from the frames, one map per kind (long, short), repaired by the 3 x 3 median of their colour plane

every frame's first guess from its own plate solve (the pre-flash frame from its neighbour, then a coarse vote); rotation + shift on the stars onto one long reference frame (20261018-102251), the short frames too (their star fluxes compared at 1/60); weighted rms at most 0.64 px long, 1.62 px short; the field turned 5.4 degrees over the used frames; air dispersion: red - green [0.3598, 0.5078], blue - green [-0.6069, -0.7637] sensor px measured in the frames and taken out in the one resampling; left in the stack: red [0.0359, 0.021], blue [0.0214, 0.0243]
every frame measured: star size, common ellipticity (smear), transparency on the stars, sky noise

steps.history: dropped: long first frame after the slew 2; long smeared 25; long stars too wide 12; long stars dimmed (cloud or haze) 5; long within 10 s of a move 1; long registration 1; short within 10 s of a move 1; short smeared 3; short stars too wide 1. Weights (transparency / noise)^2

steps.step: 6 is it the thing (reference frame plate solve)
steps.history: yes: the reference frame and the stack plate-solved (astrometry.net); theta1 Orionis C's catalogue place falls 0.9 arcsec from the brightest point near it in the stack; the brightest 2% of the reference frame's light is centred 0.13 arcmin from the Trapezium; M43's star is in the frame

small.what: green: sky small scale / flat small scale, Gaussian 4 bins of 2 x 2 plane px; a shadow left = a connected place below 1 - max(1%, 4 x the map noise) over at least 12 bins

on_m42_sky.per_colour_slope_what: the flat's deep shadows (over 4%%, at least 20 bins; up to 40): depth = 1 - mean inside 0.7 r / median of the ring r + 8 .. r + 30 px, in this sky and in the flat; the median ratio per colour. 1: as deep here as in the flat. Below 1 in one colour only: light in that colour that the dust does not shadow, or a black level set too low, by about sky x (1 - ratio) DN; above 1: the opposite

numbers.caveat: the large-scale numbers include the nebula's own light outside the mask (M42's glow fills the frame); only the small scale (dust) is a fair test here

steps.history: flat: the 13 October hybrid flat (~/.observatory/nights/2026-10-12-a6000/flat-hybrid-m77: large scale from that night's open sky, dust from the 13 October twilight flats), as tonight's M27 and M33 pipelines chose it. On this run's dithered sky (flatcheck.py, the Trapezium masked 700 px) the large-scale remainder cannot be judged: M42's glow is in every frame (G1 after a plane 0.064 for the hybrid, 0.049 for the twilight flat alone, nebula light included). Times this run's own dust measure (step 7). The short frames, 20 minutes later, get the same flat

flat_from.made_from: the night's own open sky (ngc891, ngc2261, ngc2419, m1) for the large scale; twilight flats (~/.observatory/nights/2026-10-12-a6000/flat-twilight) for dust and pixel response
flat_from.formula: flat[p] = large[p] x twilight small scale[p], 1 at the sensor centre; divide plane p (black subtracted) by it

canvas.what: canvas pixel (X, Y) = reference plane pixel (X + X0, Y + Y0)

numbers.what:
The flat: the 13 October hybrid flat (FLAT_DIR, read only: large scale from that night's open sky of NGC 891, NGC 2261,
NGC 2419 and M1; dust and pixel response from that dawn's twilight flats), chosen as tonight's M27 pipeline chose it
(it scored best on M27's open sky) and checked on this run's dithered sky in step 7a. M42's glow fills the frame, so no large
scale can be built or judged from these frames.

steps.history: dust: 12 shadows measured on this run's own long frames (each frame against the first stack put back on its sensor grid, so the nebula cancels; each seen in the first and in the second half of the run alone, 0.6% deep at least in both) and divided out, 0.96% of the sensor, deepest factor 0.852; 7 candidates turned down. The crescent at sensor (3522, 848): 11.7% deep with no flat, 12.2% left by the 13 October flat (new since then), 1.1% after this run's own correction. Not judged within 5 arcmin of the Trapezium (too bright and structured). Remainder rms on 8 px blocks 0.0048

stack.combine: long: proper coadd (coadd.py), delivered proper; control: the clipped weighted mean from the same cube; short: the clipped weighted mean

faint_region.what: area every long frame covers, darkest part of the first green stack (M42 fills the field: not the true sky)

near_ceiling.rule: at or above 0.93 x (16000 - black) raw DN in a plane of a frame, before any repair

coadd.what: proper coaddition per colour plane of the long frames; the control (the clipped weighted mean) made from the same cube

R.paper: Zackay B. & Ofek E. O. 2017, ApJ 836, 188 (arXiv:1512.06879)
R.tool: coadd.py 1.1 (2026-10-17): mean PSF phase kept, measured outlier thresholds, two-pass refill
R.formula: R_hat = sum_j (F_j/s_j^2) conj(P_hat_j) M_hat_j / sqrt(sum_j (F_j^2/s_j^2) |P_hat_j|^2); S = R / F_R, F_R = sqrt(sum_j F_j^2/s_j^2); PSF of S: P_R_hat = sqrt(sum_j (F_j^2/s_j^2) |P_hat_j|^2) / F_R
R.linear: given the outlier mask, S is linear in the frames; the weights and filters come from the PSFs and the noise only

outliers.rule: flag |X_j - m| > kappa sqrt(r_j^2 + (beta m)^2) per pixel, or |B(X_j - m)| > kappa_smooth sqrt(b_j^2 + (beta B(m))^2) with B a 3 x 3 box mean; grow 1 px; X_j = frame / F_j, m the per-pixel median of all frames that have the pixel, r_j and b_j the robust (1.4826 MAD) spread of X_j - m and of B(X_j - m) over the frame, times noise_map
outliers.beta_why: from the PSFs: the largest peak ratio to the median is 1.473; beta = max(0.50, 2 x 0.473 / kappa)

target.target: mean-psf: |sum_j w_j P_hat_j| / sum_j w_j, w_j = F_j^2 / s_j^2 (a weighted mean's PSF, its phase dropped)

field_variation.rule: varies if the zones differ by > 3 x the halves' noise and by > 3% in HFD or > 0.05 in ellipticity

to_common.target: the minimum of the full set's and both halves' P_R_hat, with the full set's phase

steps.history: long: proper coaddition (Zackay & Ofek 2017; tools/coadd.py, keep_phase="mean"), one PSF per frame and plane from 72 stars (green), outlier mask; delivered: proper. Short: the 3-sigma clipped weighted mean (the control's code) of the 44 short frames. Sky: ONE constant per colour per frame: the clipped mean over the darkest 30% of the area every long frame covers. M42 fills the field: the zero is the faintest part of the field, not the true sky; no surface fitted

blend.rim: short value blurred (sigma 2) below 5 sigma of its own noise, sharp above 20

steps.history: the short stack replaces the long one wherever any long frame came within 7 percent of the ceiling (any plane), grown one colour cell, with a smooth ramp in brightness (10,000 to 14,000 DN as the sensor saw it) so there is no step; factor 62.645 measured on the nebula (65.17 on stars) against 60 expected

steps.step: 9 coverage, plate solve of the stack, star colours, render

sun_like_stars.rule: BP - RP 0.72 to 0.92, linear sRGB through the camera matrix; white is 1, 1

colour_term.per: mag of residual per mag of BP - RP, all measured stars 0.3 to 2.0 not clipped

catalogue.name: Gaia DR3
catalogue.epoch: positions at 2016.0 (ICRS); move them with the proper motions to the night

colour.reference_white: the Sun's colour (Gaia BP - RP 0.82) is white
colour.model: BP - RP -> T (Mucciarelli & Bellazzini 2020, dwarfs) -> black body -> CIE 1931 (Wyman et al. 2013 fits) -> linear sRGB; measured: camera RGB x (kR, 1, kB) -> render.py camera matrix -> linear sRGB

aperture.ceiling_rule: peak / wb + sky (RAW DN) under 60% of 15488

steps.history: cut to 2820 x 1948 px = 36.5 x 25.2 arcmin, the largest upright rectangle where at least half the long frames have data; inside it 65% of pixels have every long frame and 86% at least three quarters. Colour: camera daylight white balance x Gaia DR3 star colours (kR 0.9881, kB 1.1750 from 13 stars), the camera's own colour matrix; colour only where the light carries it; where even the short frames came near the ceiling, white

steps.how: brightness changed, each pixel's colour ratios kept

steps.brightness: bilateral filter, sigma 3.0 px, 7 L units
steps.where: full below L 10, none above L 40 (brightness judged on a blurred copy)

steps.left_alone: below L 6 (fading in to L 20) and above L 93
steps.sky_without_colour: colour fades to grey below L 8 (full colour from L 20): the dark sky's colour is noise

numbers.what:
Each half's green, stars taken out (every source of the reference frame masked and filled with the smooth light, then a
5 x 5 median on a 2 x 2 binned copy), then band-passed to the scale of arms and
clusters (Gaussian SIG_LO px minus Gaussian SIG_HI px). In tiles of TILE arcmin across the picture: the correlation of
the two halves' band-passed light, and the same with one half turned by 180 degrees about the tile's centre (the null:
noise and leftover stars agree with nothing). A tile passes if its correlation is above the null's mean + 5 x the
null's spread over all tiles. The tiles are binned by distance from the Trapezium: the outer loops are the far ones. The
faintest tiles (the lowest third of the stack's smoothed green) are reported on their own: that is the faint outer light.

solve.command: solve-field --config ~/.observatory/astrometry/astrometry.cfg --overwrite --no-plots --no-remove-lines --uniformize 0 --width 2820 --height 1948 --x-column X --y-column Y --sort-column FLUX --scale-units arcsecperpix --scale-low 0.72 --scale-high 0.84 --ra 83.8186 --dec -5.3897 --radius 1 --cpulimit 120 --tweak-order 2 -N none --rdls none --match none --solved none --index-xyls none --corr img.corr --wcs img.wcs img.xy

wcs_check.what: "within a pixel or two": passes with at least 20 stars, median <= 1.5 px, 90th percentile <= 2.5 px, mean offset <= 1 px each way. Isolated Gaia DR3 stars (G < 16.0, proper motion to 2026.80) looked for at their places through the WCS: intensity-weighted 9 x 9 px centroid, three moves, peak above 15 x the noise, unsaturated, within 4 px

software_note: the versions in this environment when the recipe was brought to the schema; the packages were installed before the night and not changed since
method_note: deterministic array arithmetic only: averages, medians, measured fits, fixed curves and matrices. Nothing generative, learned or upscaled
template: hack/stacks/2026-10-17/m33 (calibration on a canvas), hack/stacks/2026-10-17/m27 (proper coaddition with the old mean as a control), hack/stacks/2026-10-03/m42 (the long + short join)

summary.frames: 241 frames on M42 in the windows (by the RAW's own EXIF and each frame's own plate solve): 193 long (30 s ISO 1600, the one before the firmware flash included), 48 short (2 s ISO 400); used 165 long and 44 short
summary.dropped_note: a frame can be dropped for more than one reason; every frame's own reasons are under "dropped"
not_in_the_run: centring frames (2 s, ISO 6400, 09:00 and 09:01 UTC) and the 15 s ISO 3200 frames of M33 before 08:56 lie outside the windows
the last short frame (12:16:18) has a sidecar but no RAW on disk; it was never read
summary.integration: long 165 x 30 s = 82.5 minutes; short 44 x 2 s = 88 s
summary.star_size: half-flux diameter, green: 6.41 arcsec in the joined stack (52 compact stars), 6.46 in the reference frame alone; median of the unsmeared long frames 6.19, short 6.50; the proper coadd's PSF 8.22 px = 6.38 arcsec against the control's 8.27 px
summary.registration: every frame's first guess from its own plate solve (the pre-flash frame from its neighbour, then a coarse vote); rotation + shift on the stars onto one long reference frame (20261018-102251), the short frames too (their star fluxes compared at 1/60); weighted rms at most 0.64 px long, 1.62 px short; the field turned 5.4 degrees over the used frames
summary.flat: the 13 October hybrid flat (~/.observatory/nights/2026-10-12-a6000/flat-hybrid-m77: large scale from that night's open sky, dust from the 13 October twilight flats), as tonight's M27 and M33 pipelines chose it. On this run's dithered sky (flatcheck.py, the Trapezium masked 700 px) the large-scale remainder cannot be judged: M42's glow is in every frame (G1 after a plane 0.064 for the hybrid, 0.049 for the twilight flat alone, nebula light included). Times this run's own dust measure (step 7). The short frames, 20 minutes later, get the same flat
summary.dust: 12 shadows measured on this run's own long frames (each frame against the first stack put back on its sensor grid, so the nebula cancels; each seen in the first and in the second half of the run alone, 0.6% deep at least in both) and divided out, 0.96% of the sensor, deepest factor 0.852; 7 candidates turned down. The crescent at sensor (3522, 848): 11.7% deep with no flat, 12.2% left by the 13 October flat (new since then), 1.1% after this run's own correction. Not judged within 5 arcmin of the Trapezium (too bright and structured). Remainder rms on 8 px blocks 0.0048
summary.darks: none: darks.subtract changed nothing and said so; hot pixels found from the frames, one map per kind (long, short), repaired by the 3 x 3 median of their colour plane

combine.long: proper coaddition (Zackay & Ofek 2017; tools/coadd.py, keep_phase="mean"), one PSF per frame and plane from 72 stars (green), outlier mask; delivered: proper
combine.control: the old 3-sigma clipped weighted mean from the same cube, in the same pass
combine.short: the 3-sigma clipped weighted mean (the control's code) of the 44 short frames

join.rule: the short stack replaces the long one wherever any long frame came within 7 percent of the ceiling (any plane), grown one colour cell, with a smooth ramp in brightness (10,000 to 14,000 DN as the sensor saw it) so there is no step

summary.sky: ONE constant per colour per frame: the clipped mean over the darkest 30% of the area every long frame covers. M42 fills the field: the zero is the faintest part of the field, not the true sky; no surface fitted
summary.air_dispersion: red - green [0.3598, 0.5078], blue - green [-0.6069, -0.7637] sensor px measured in the frames and taken out in the one resampling; left in the stack: red [0.0359, 0.021], blue [0.0214, 0.0243]
summary.noise: green per pixel in the faint region (stars masked; this region is faint nebula, so its own texture is in these numbers): proper coadd 4.51 DN, control 4.54, the reference frame alone 38.73; the noise alone, from half the difference of the odd and even coadds, 3.01 DN (12.9 x under the single frame, against sqrt(165) = 12.8); the short stack 1.05 in its own units
